links.outcome: Workflow reliability and unintended consequences observed during a limited pilot of AI fracture detection
links.effect: The 2-month pilot exposed delayed or missing AI results, provider confusion when AI and radiologist reads differed, and workflow inconsistency that aggregate performance did not capture.
links.quote: In our experience, aggregate performance alone did not capture the practical issues most relevant to clinical adoption, including delayed or missing AI results, provider confusion when AI and radiologist interpretations differed, and the infrastructure required for sustainable oversight.

links.outcome: Infrastructure and resource burden of post-deployment monitoring of the AI tool
links.effect: Value was limited by cost, false-positive and false-negative results, workflow inconsistency, and the burden of post-deployment monitoring.
links.quote: Although the tool was sometimes helpful, particularly for subtle fractures and as confirmatory support in borderline cases, its overall value was limited by cost, false-positive and false-negative results, workflow inconsistency, and the burden of post-deployment monitoring.

screen.reason: Reports on a 2-month real-world trial of a commercial AI fracture detection tool in a pediatric hospital, focusing on clinical utility, workflow, and deployment challenges, but does not compare specific deployment practices.
